title: Integrating neuroplasticity into whole-brain modeling: From synapses to neural populations
title_zh: 将神经可塑性整合到全脑建模：从突触到神经群体
abstract: The brain's ability to learn, adapt, and recover hinges on synaptic plasticity, yet most large-scale neural models overlook this core feature. In this review, we argue that embedding plasticity is essential for the simulation of realistic population-level brain activity. To this end, we explore specific computational attempts at scaling microscopic single-neuron plasticity rules to mesoscopic populations, drawing from mechanistic insights into short-term synaptic dynamics, long-term potentiation, and homeostatic regulation. We also discuss how plasticity mechanisms in neural field and neural mass models can potentially help us understand recovery trajectories, and how dysfunctional plasticity can play a role in them. Finally, we review state-of-the-art multiscale co-simulations methods that bridge spiking neuron networks with neural field and mass models and discuss their ability to link microscopic synaptic mechanisms with macroscopic brain dynamics. By embedding plasticity as a core feature, we can develop mean-field models that are more realistic and powerful tools for understanding brain function and recovery.
abstract_zh: 大脑的学习、适应和恢复能力依赖于突触可塑性，然而大多数大规模神经模型都忽略了这一核心特性。在本综述中，我们论证嵌入可塑性对于模拟真实的群体水平脑活动至关重要。为此，我们探索了将微观单神经元可塑性规则扩展到中观群体的具体计算尝试，引入了短期突触动力学、长时程增强和家态调节的机制见解。我们还讨论了神经场和神经群体模型中可塑性机制如何潜在地帮助我们理解恢复轨迹，以及功能障碍性可塑性在这些过程中的作用。最后，我们综述了将突触神经网络与神经场和群体模型桥接的前沿多尺度耦合模拟方法，并讨论了它们将微观突触机制与宏观脑动力学联系起来的能力。通过将可塑性作为核心特性，我们可以开发出更真实、更强大的均值场模型，用于理解脑功能和恢复。
